methodological_note_on_text_search: Raw CSV text searches for markers such as 'pp.:' produce duplicated textual hits because the same note can be serialized in more than one field. Therefore raw marker-hit counts are not treated as unique lexical annotation counts. Unique Pp counts here use the classification fields instead.

key_source_explicit_examples.significance: The source explicitly identifies the final-ami form as pp even though the derived entry itself is not classified Pp. Pp-field counts therefore undercount source-explicit participial evidence.
Classification and explicit source note independently converge on Comíami as participial.
Directly strengthens the morphological side of the historical Tſchiperameke ~ modern Chipérami comparison.
Internal minimal contrast: the source itself distinguishes an -ami adjective from a -cami participle in the same lexical family. Therefore final -ami cannot be equated mechanically with pp.
Direct source-explicit simple -ami participle comparable in broad function to historical Cotſchimé ~ Cotſchimeameke. No cognacy judgment is made here.
Another direct source-explicit X~X+ami participial relation.

interpretation: SRC-02 gives direct source-level evidence that -ami participates in participial formations, but also direct evidence that final -ami is not synonymous with the category Pp. The safest model is a broad surface -ami domain containing source-tagged participles alongside adjectives, nouns, adverbs and possibly lexicalized derivatives. Source-explicit Pp evidence must be separated from string-final distribution and from semantic derivational inference.
